questions.text: A multi-purpose community hall is designed with temporary wooden stages for barangay events and political rallies. What is the occupancy classification of this facility?

options.text: Group A (Residential), which is typically not applicable to community halls used for public events
Group C (Education and Recreation), which may apply if the hall is used for educational purposes
Group E (Business and Mercantile), which is generally not suitable for assembly uses

rationale.a: Group A is residential; community halls are not residential.
rationale.b: Group C (theater/auditorium) applies to permanent-stage venues with designed-in theater seating. This facility has temporary stages, so it is Group H.
rationale.d: Group E is mercantile/business; community halls are assembly, not commercial.
rationale.correct: A multi-purpose hall with temporary stages serving varied community functions is Group H (assembly). Group H applies to general-purpose assembly venues. If it had a permanent stage designed specifically as a theater/auditorium, it would be Group H, Division 1. (NBC Occupancy Groups, ERR-DSGN-005 inverse)
rationale.takeaway: Multi-purpose hall with temporary stages = Group H (Assembly). Permanent theater stage = Group C.

questions.text: A 350-sqm multi-purpose hall (Group H assembly) is not sprinklered. What is the maximum allowed travel distance to an exit?

rationale.a: 30 meters is more restrictive than required.
rationale.c: 60 meters applies only to sprinklered buildings; this hall is unsprinklered.
rationale.correct: For Group H assembly without sprinklers, maximum travel distance = 45 meters per NBC. Sprinklered buildings may extend to 60 meters. (NBC Fire Safety, Travel Distance)
rationale.takeaway: Unsprinklered Group H assembly: max travel distance = 45 meters. Sprinklered = 60 meters.

questions.text: A multi-purpose hall is arranged for standing-room-only capacity. How much floor area per person is required for standing occupancy?

rationale.a: 0.5 sqm/person is too dense and does not meet NBC clearance requirements.
rationale.c: 1.0 sqm/person is looser than required; standing is 0.65 sqm/person.
rationale.d: 1.1 sqm/person is for seated occupancy with folding chairs, not standing.
rationale.correct: Standing-room occupancy density = 0.65 sqm per person per NBC assembly standards. This allows for body space and minimal movement clearance. (PD 1096 Rule VIII, Table VIII.3.1 Occupant Load Factors)
rationale.takeaway: Standing-room occupancy = 0.65 sqm per person per NBC.

questions.text: A multi-purpose hall with 272-person seated occupancy (Group H assembly) requires a minimum combined exit width. Calculate using 7.6 mm/person per NBC Table 3.

rationale.a: 1.36 m uses 5 mm/person; NBC specifies 7.6 mm/person.
rationale.b: 1.63 m uses 6 mm/person; correct rate is 7.6 mm/person.
rationale.d: 2.72 m uses 10 mm/person; NBC requires 7.6 mm/person.
rationale.correct: Exit width = Occupant load × 7.6 mm/person ÷ 1000 = 272 × 7.6 ÷ 1000 = 2.067 m ≈ 2.07 m. (NBC Table 3, ERR-DSGN-019 inverse)
rationale.takeaway: Exit width = Occupant load × 7.6 mm/person per NBC Table 3.

questions.text: A multi-purpose hall plans to store 200 folding chairs. What is the minimum floor area required for chair storage?

rationale.a: 10 sqm uses 0.05 sqm/chair; correct standard is 0.1 sqm/chair.
rationale.c: 30 sqm exceeds the requirement; 20 sqm is the standard.
rationale.d: 40 sqm is twice the required amount.
rationale.correct: Chair storage density = 0.1 sqm per folding chair. For 200 chairs: 200 × 0.1 = 20 sqm. (NBC Assembly Storage Standards)
rationale.takeaway: Folding chair storage = 0.1 sqm per chair. For 200 chairs: 20 sqm.

questions.text: A demountable (temporary) stage is to be installed in a multi-purpose hall. What is the required minimum depth?

rationale.a: 2.0–3.0 meters is too shallow for performer movement and equipment.
rationale.c: 6.0–8.0 meters is larger than standard demountable requirement.
rationale.d: 8.0–10.0 meters exceeds typical temporary stage depth.
rationale.correct: Demountable stage depth = 4.0–6.0 meters to accommodate performers, technical setup, and minimal storage. (NBC Assembly Stage Standards)
rationale.takeaway: Demountable stage depth = 4.0–6.0 meters per assembly standards.

questions.text: What is the correct height range for a permanent stage in a multi-purpose hall per standard design practice?

rationale.a: 300–400 mm is too low for audience visibility.
rationale.b: 450–550 mm is below the recommended range.
rationale.d: 800–900 mm exceeds standard and creates greater fall risk.
rationale.correct: Permanent stage height = 600–750 mm above floor level. This height ensures stage visibility for seated audiences without creating excessive fall hazard. (NBC Assembly Stage Standards)
rationale.takeaway: Permanent stage height = 600–750 mm per assembly design standards.

questions.text: A community hall designed as a permanent theater with a fixed stage, theater seating, and projection equipment should be classified as which occupancy group?

options.text: Group H (Assembly) because it has seating, which is a primary characteristic of assembly occupancies
Group E (Business and Mercantile) because it is commercial, focusing on the business aspect of theater operations
Group H, Division 1 (Assembly with stage) (ERR-DSGN-005 inverse)
Group A (Residential), assuming it serves as a temporary living space for performers

rationale.a: Group H applies to general assembly venues with temporary/flexible stages; permanent theaters are Group C.
rationale.b: Group E is mercantile/commercial office; theaters are Group C.
rationale.d: Group A is residential; theaters are not residential.
rationale.correct: A purpose-built theater with a permanent stage, designed theater seating, and entertainment infrastructure is Group C (education and recreation), not Group H. This distinction affects exit capacity and occupancy calculations. (NBC Occupancy Groups, ERR-DSGN-005)
rationale.takeaway: Permanent theater with fixed stage = Group C. Multi-purpose hall with temporary stage = Group H. (ERR-DSGN-005)

questions.text: An accessible wheelchair seating area in a multi-purpose hall must be sized to accommodate one wheelchair user and one companion. What are the minimum dimensions per BP 344?

options.text: 2.5m × 3.0m, which allows for additional maneuvering space beyond the minimum requirements
3.0m × 4.0m, providing ample space for both users and additional equipment if necessary
4.5m × 6.0m, ensuring maximum comfort and accessibility for all users

rationale.a: 2.5m × 3.0m is too small for wheelchair and companion.
rationale.b: 3.0m × 4.0m does not meet the required dimensions.
rationale.correct: Accessible wheelchair seating area per BP 344 = 4.0m × 5.0m per wheelchair plus companion. This accommodates wheelchair maneuverability and companion seating. (BP 344 Accessibility Standards)
rationale.takeaway: Accessible wheelchair seating area per BP 344 = 4.0m × 5.0m.

questions.text: A 300-sqm multi-purpose hall is arranged with folding chairs for seated occupancy. At 1.1 sqm per seated person, what is the maximum occupant load?

rationale.a: 195 persons uses incorrect divisor (1.5); correct is 1.1.
rationale.c: 330 persons uses 0.9; seated chairs are 1.1 sqm/person.
rationale.d: 450 persons is for standing (0.65 sqm/person), not seated.
rationale.correct: Occupant load = Hall area ÷ area per person = 300 sqm ÷ 1.1 sqm/person = 272.7 persons (round to 272). (NBC Assembly Occupancy Calculation)
rationale.takeaway: Seated occupancy = Hall area ÷ 1.1 sqm/person. For 300 sqm: 272 persons.
